Eligibility: This role is open to INSEAD 26D students, IE MBAs graduating between Dec 2026 - Mar 2027, and second year MBA students from ESADE, IESE, HEC, and LBS, who are seeking full-time roles.

Boston Consulting Group partners with leaders in business and society to tackle their most important challenges and capture their greatest opportunities. BCG was the pioneer in business strategy when it was founded in 1963. Today, we help clients with total transformation-inspiring complex change, enabling organizations to grow, building competitive advantage, and driving bottom-line impact.

To succeed, organizations must blend digital and human capabilities. Our diverse, global teams bring deep industry and functional expertise and a range of perspectives to spark change. BCG delivers solutions through leading-edge management consulting along with technology and design, corporate and digital ventures-and business purpose. We work in a uniquely collaborative model across the firm and throughout all levels of the client organization, generating results that allow our clients to thrive.

notes:
Rebuilt 2026-09-04. The version before this dated from 08-26 and had three problems independent of content: it put three points each under Valeo and EverHaus, breaking the standing cap that an internship and a part-time role must not outweigh the full-time ones; it predated valeo-cost-buyin, nutanix-move-diligence and nutanix-vp-roadmap, so the CEO-approval beat and the technical due diligence were simply absent; and its Skills line was the profile default reordered ("Leadership | Project Management | Budget and Resource Management...") with Quantum Computing still sitting in Technologies, which is noise to a consulting reader. It also carried a repeated-phrase finding ("product roadmap" across everhaus-roadmap and eleven01-mvp).

The scorer is effectively blind on this JD - it is BCG eligibility text plus firm boilerplate, so only strategy-consulting fires (3.25) and everything else lands between 0 and 3. Ranking discarded; this is judgement, recorded here to be argued with.

What BCG asks for that Bain did not: "blend digital and human capabilities", "technology and design, corporate and digital ventures", "driving bottom-line impact". Parag technical depth is worth more here than on the Bain generalist CV, so the digital signal is carried four times over (valeo-cost-diagnosis on cursor-forward, everhaus-operating-model AI-first, nutanix-ai-workflow, and Claude/Cursor/MCP leading Technologies) rather than being left to the Skills line.

Valeo is diagnosis plus the merged buy-in override, the same pair and the same overrideText as both Bain CVs: capping Valeo at two forces a choice between the 30% recommendation and the CEO approval, and the override carries both facts with valeo-cost-strategy off the page so nothing is double-counted. valeo-route-app is the loss worth naming - "built it end-to-end with AI, 100% adoption in one week" is the single best bullet for BCG "blend digital and human capabilities" phrase, but the cap allows two and dropping valeo-cost-diagnosis would leave the CV with no data-analysis coverage at all.

EverHaus is compliance plus operating-model rather than compliance plus roadmap: the operating-model bullet is the venture-flavoured one (AI-first operating model, demo product, investor conversations) and dropping everhaus-roadmap also clears the "product roadmap" collision with eleven01-mvp, so eleven01-mvp can run on zero-to-one without an override here.

nutanix-sales-acv is on customer-forward, not xfn-forward. xfn-forward reads better for BCG "uniquely collaborative model" and was what the old CV used, but it wraps to two lines and that line is worth more spent on nutanix-move-diligence. touchnote-checkout replaces touchnote-new-revenue: the CV is already dense with revenue figures, and Conversion Rate / Average Order Value / Cart Abandonment is the one place Parag shows customer-metric fluency and the only consumer-facing story on an otherwise B2B page.

No em-dashes render on this page (checked).
